endorsements.quote: Local validation AI models should be tested in the target population before clinical use.

However, successful implementation requires harmonized imaging protocols, local validation, quality-control procedures, regulatory compliance, data protection safeguards and multidisciplinary agreement on how AI-derived metrics should inform clinical decisions.

unlisted_practices: Implement quality control with visual overlays and expert review to detect segmentation or slice-selection errors in AI body composition analysis.
Standardize imaging acquisition protocols and analytical protocols, including L3 slice selection and tissue segmentation, for AI-based body composition analysis.
Conduct large-scale multicenter, real-world external validation of AI body composition tools across different oncological populations.
Interpret body composition cut-off thresholds as supportive rather than prescriptive and do not use adipose tissue metrics as stand-alone decision thresholds.
Conduct prospective studies showing AI-based body composition decisions improve relevant outcomes before using them for treatment dosing personalization.
Use single-slice L3 analysis primarily for baseline phenotyping and interpret longitudinal changes cautiously with clinical, nutritional and functional measures.

screen.reason: This is an opinion paper examining the clinical integration, benefits, and governance/implementation gaps of AI-based body composition assessment in routine oncology.
